newsitem.title: USA: Plains fed cattle sales thin at $72 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains fed cattle sales thin at $72 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Wednesday traded in light volume at $72.00 per cwt, unchanged from Tuesday and last week's top in central and southern areas, feedlot sources said.
About 1,600 head sold in Kansas and 3,800 in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area, sources there noted. The sales were "clean-up" activity following Tuesday's brisk trade.
Most feedlot showlists in Kansas and a large percentage of Panhandle showlists were sold as packers continued to ensure they had inventory to meet strong beef demand, sources said.
Tight supplies of well-finished cattle that will grade choice continued to be reflected in the price spread between choice and select grade beef, sources said.

Beef prices at midday were quoted up $0.26 to $0.34 per cwt for choice supplies but select-grade beef prices fell $0.54 to $0.55, USDA said. The agency reported sales on 230 fabricated loads at midday.
Heavyweight choice beef was quoted up $0.26 at $115.86, up $3.12 from Friday's quote.
